narrative.overview: Painless is a dark room where the media performs. The interface is the theater's architecture — walls, wings, and an inspector's rail — built so that nothing competes with the photograph or the frame on stage. Chrome recedes: surfaces are black or near-black panels, separated by 1px hairlines rather than shadows, and the brightest surface on any screen is the media itself. The system's one structural indulgence is the inspector rail: a fixed 300px column of quiet, right-aligned facts that sits beside the stage like production notes taped to the wing. Density is high but calm: micro-labels at 9-10px uppercase with wide letter-spacing, UI text at 11-14px, and generous structural padding around content zones. Depth is never faked with glow — a surface is either a different tonal step or it is divided by a hairline.
keyCharacteristics: Flat black surfaces, 1px hairline borders, zero shadows
Monochrome primary accent (near-white on dark, near-black on light); blue reserved for tags/info
Fixed inspector rail (300px) for metadata; media stage takes all remaining space
Small, quiet UI type (9-14px) with uppercase micro-labels at 700-800 weight
Tonal layering for elevation (BgBase → BgContainer → BgElevated → fills)

rules.name: The Receding Chrome Rule
rules.body: No structural surface may be brighter than Raised Panel (#1a1a1a) in dark mode. If a UI element draws more attention than the media beside it, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Monochrome Voice Rule
rules.body: The primary accent is grayscale. Chromatic color (blue, green, amber, red) speaks only for meaning — status, format, information — never for style. If a colored element carries no semantic job, make it ink.

rules.name: The Small Chrome Rule
rules.body: Interface text lives between 9px and 14px. Larger sizes are reserved for content titles and the drive identity — never for buttons or labels.

rules.name: The Flat Stage Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast shadows. A new layer earns presence by one tonal step up (or a hairline), never by elevation.

dos: Do consume Lobe tokens (tk.*) for every color, radius, and font size — no hardcoded hex in UI code.
Do build chrome as borderless bars and rows with 1px hairline dividers; let the media own the brightest pixels.
Do use tonal steps (BgBase → BgContainer → BgElevated) or hairlines for depth; state changes use alpha fills (10-16%).
Do verify renders in dark mode (the flagship) at narrow widths — 800×600 viewer and 922px catalog are the regression checkpoints.
Do keep UI text at 9-14px and create hierarchy with weight, case, and letter-spacing.
donts: Don't design like a website — no boxed cards around player controls, no per-row icons in the metadata rail, no web-page chrome (boxed headers, pill toolbars). This is a binding product commitment.
Don't add box-shadows or glow; the system is flat by construction.
Don't use chromatic color decoratively — blue is for tags/info, green/amber/red are semantic only.
Don't let structural chrome exceed Raised Panel (#1a1a1a) in dark mode.
Don't wrap the inspector rail or stack it below the stage; it is a fixed 300px column that squeezes the stage.
